subject: Structural Budget Deficit and FY23 Submission
overview: The Council received the Mayor's proposed $201.1 million FY2023 budget but tabled it pending further review, while passing a suite of resolutions aimed at addressing the city's structural deficit and financial transparency.

items.title: Public Hearing on Extended Hours at 61 Locust Street
items.summary: Approved a special permit for Ford on the Meadow to extend its hours of operation from 11:00 p.m. to 1:00 a.m.

items.title: Zoning Change Request for 196-200 Boston Avenue
items.summary: Referred a request from Cummings Properties LLC to rezone two parcels from Industrial to Office 2 to the Community Development Board.

items.title: Food Truck Permit Application for Riverside Plaza
items.summary: Tabled a request for a pop-up coffee cart for one week to determine if the proposal complies with city ordinances and to assess the impact on nearby brick-and-mortar businesses.

items.title: Fiscal Year 2023 Budget Submission
items.summary: Tabled the Mayor's proposed $201,154,843 operating budget for one week and requested hard copies of the budget book for council members.

items.title: Sidewalk and Infrastructure Hazards at 101 Sydney Street
items.summary: Discussed reports of sinking sidewalks and inadequate drainage causing resident injuries, and referred the matter to next week's agenda to request attendance from the city engineer and DPW.

items.title: Routine Business, Minutes, and Ceremonial Resolutions
items.summary: Approved meeting records, committee reports on the budget, and a resolution offering condolences for Richard Edward Fitzpatrick Sr.

items.title: Tick Remediation Program
items.summary: Requested that the Board of Health establish a tick remediation program for city parks and open spaces and report back on associated costs.

items.title: Independent Outside Audit and Financial Oversight
items.summary: Approved a resolution requesting an independent outside audit of all municipal and school departments and a meeting with bond counsel to discuss the city's indebtedness.

items.title: Revenue Planning and ARPA Fund Accounting
items.summary: Approved a series of resolutions requiring the city to release a 10-year revenue generation plan and a full accounting of all ARPA funds spent or remaining.

items.title: Proposition 2 1/2 Override and Deficit Mitigation
items.summary: Requested the administration demonstrate in writing how the city will resolve its structural deficit and avoid service cuts in the FY24 budget without a Proposition 2 1/2 override.

items.title: MBTA Bus Redesign and Communication Accessibility
items.summary: Approved resolutions requesting the MBTA solicit feedback on bus network changes from senior facilities and asking the DEI Director to ensure city communications reach residents without internet access.

items.title: Fines and Fees Revenue Feasibility Study
items.summary: Requested an analysis from the administration on the feasibility of increasing certain fines and fees to create recurring revenue to offset the budgetary gap.
